question: Let $n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_{51}$ be distinct natural numbers each of which has exactly $2023$ positive integer factors. For instance, $2^{2022}$ has exactly $2023$ positive integer factors $1,2,2^2,\ldots,2^{2021},2^{2022}$. Assume that no prime larger than $11$ divides any of the $n_i$'s. Show that there must be some perfect cube among the $n_i$'s. You may use the fact that $2023=7\times17\times17$.
